correctness.rationale: Every block is finite-dimensional, reflexive and strictly convex, and the Hilbert sum preserves reflexivity and strict convexity. In block n, the coordinate vectors are exactly Birkhoff–James orthogonal and both sum/difference norms equal 2^(1/p_n), which tends to two as p_n decreases to one. Hence the orthogonal profile is at least two in the supremum and cannot exceed the classical triangle-inequality bound two; all approximate profiles are squeezed to the same value. If a unit pair attained James value two, both sum and difference norms would equal two; strict convexity would force simultaneously x=y and x=-y, impossible.

final_claim: The reflexive strictly convex Hilbert sum of the planes l_{1+1/n}^2 has orthogonal and approximate Birkhoff–James profiles equal to the classical James value two for every approximation parameter below one, hence zero saturation, while no unit pair attains the value two.
